title: Linked List Cycle II
summary: Return the node where a linked list's cycle begins, or null if the list has no cycle, using O(1) extra space.

tests.explain: The tail (7) links back to index 1, so the cycle starts at the node holding 9. Return that node (the tests compare its value).
The second node links back to the head, so the cycle starts at the head.

hints: First find out whether there is a cycle at all: run slow and fast pointers until they meet or fast reaches null.
Let F be the distance from the head to the cycle entry. When the pointers meet, the meeting point is exactly F steps (plus some whole laps) before the entry.
So put one pointer back on the head, leave the other at the meeting point, and move both one step at a time. They meet at the entry.

complexity.time: O(n): two walks, each shorter than the list plus one lap
